resolutions.note: Took the narrowing, per the coordinator's routing note, not the 'name it' half of the acceptance line: listing->detail is the most common navigation shape in this domain and a guard that breaks it would cost more correct-answer rate than the defect it fixes. `not_page_furniture` (src/browser/verifier.py) now compares `_context(page_text, value, PAGE_CONTEXT_WINDOW=20)` -- the value plus 20 raw chars either side of it, from the page it was read from -- against `other_page_text`, instead of the bare value. Site chrome is one repeated template fragment and carries its neighbours with it wherever it recurs (shop.html's row reads 'Aurora Desk Lamp $39.00'; that product's own detail page reads 'Aurora Desk Lamp $39.00 LAMP-STD Anodised aluminium...' -- the window diverges within a few characters); a coincidentally-repeated fact does not. The numeric exemption is deleted outright, not narrowed -- it was covering for the mechanism being too broad, not for numbers being special, and the context compare handles tc2-shop-search-zh's $18.00 and trap-near-miss-entity's $59.00 correctly with the SAME rule, closing the numeric-furniture ceiling D24 previously declared rather than widening it, exactly the 'one rule handles both' signal the routing note asked to check for. PAGE_CONTEXT_WINDOW=20 was swept (10-60) against all four known shapes (this title case, both price cases, and the original 'Travel'/'Warning!' furniture) -- every width in that range agrees on all four, 20 sits in the middle. nav-heavy-home.html (the fixture verifier-responsive-not-page-furniture navigates from) was widened from a one-item sidebar to the full 35-item list identical to nav-heavy.html's, matching books.toscrape.com's own shape (re-confirmed live by curl: the same ~50-category sidebar, same order, on every page) -- a fixture where only the bare STRING repeated, not its neighbours, could not have exercised a context-window check honestly.
resolutions.red_watched: New case verifier-listing-detail-title-not-furniture (shop.html -> shop-lamp-std.html, click 'Aurora Desk Lamp' then extract the product's own <h1>) run against the pre-repair (bare-value + numeric-exemption) code: status failure:semantic, verdict FAIL, checks.not_page_furniture false, reason 'value also appears verbatim on a different page this run visited, which is page chrome, not a page-specific answer: ["Aurora Desk Lamp"]' -- despite answer_matches: true (the correct answer). The reviewer's own synthetic repro against verify() directly reproduced the same result before the fix: not_page_furniture=False, verdict=FAIL for 'The Great Gatsby'.
resolutions.green_after: Same new case, and the reviewer's exact repro, both pass after the narrowing: `python3 -c "...verify(...'The Great Gatsby'...)" -> True PASS`. tc2-shop-search-zh and trap-near-miss-entity re-verified to keep their original expected shape (trap-near-miss-entity: status success at runtime, only ground-truth L2 catches the wrong answer -- unaffected by the narrowing, confirming the numeric exemption's removal did not change what this trap is measuring).
resolutions.confirmed_original_defect_still_fails: verifier-responsive-not-page-furniture (the 'Travel' shape) and the R1 finding's own repro-equivalent for 'Warning!' were both re-run after the narrowing: not_page_furniture still returns False / verdict FAIL for both -- the sidebar and banner still carry their neighbours with them because they are the same repeated fragment on every page, which is exactly what the context compare is built to catch. Not asserted from reasoning alone: re-run and read the actual checks dict both before and after the change (see red_watched/green_after above).
